body:
Actually, it was a unintended change. Sorry about that.
Anyway, Yes. I think it should be a `ETIMEDOUT`. 

As a axios consumer, There's no reliable ways to know given request was timed out or not. Current error does not help consumers to detect timeouts easily. Currently, It only can be done by matching error message like below:

```typescript
const isTimeoutError = /timed?out/i.test(error.message);
// or
const isTimeoutError = error.message.includes("timeout");
```

I think it is not reliable way to match timeout errors. 

Another reason why we should change error code is for clarity. `ETIMEDOUT` error code is more clearer than `ECONNABORTED`. because timeout was really happened so that's why we aborted request. I also think `ECONNABORTED` is not actual root cause of given error.

Final reason why we should change error code is for consistency. Node.js built-in modules use `ETIMEDOUT` error code for timeout errors.

body: Actually, `HTTPRequest#setTimeout` cannot detect connect timeout. I'm not sure it's intended or just a bug of Node.js core. Current `HTTPRequest#setTimeout` implementation won't call `Socket#setTimeout` internally if connect timeout was happened. Please refer to https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v13.12.0/lib/_http_client.js#L808-L812 . You'll notice `Socket#setTimeout` will not be called until connection establish.

author: chinesedfan

body:
Yes, this is correct, the proxy protocol should follow the proxy config. The proxy connection should use the protocol specified in the proxy config (e.g., https://proxy.com). Once a connection to the proxy has been established, then original request is sent using the request protocol.

Here's the real world scenario I ran into originally. At work I'm behind a corporate proxy that only supports HTTP.

```
http_proxy=http://corporate.com
https_proxy=http://corporate.com
```

body:
it's an edge case, really - people do the weirdest things in their project's package.json (as my own example showed). the fix is simple enough, the package.json just has to be valid and meet the minimum requirements (the version should be there at all times, technically - til).

yet, this issue might highlight a completely different problem. relying on the validity of / bundling the package.json might not be the best solution to use a version for negotiation (as seen in this PR) nor to be used for the user agent (as seen in the linked issue above where it is [imported in the http adapter](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/lib/adapters/http.js#L13)).

is this actually a path/loader issue and the version to be read is the one from axios' own package.json, not the project's? looking at the http adapter code it looks like it wants [axios' version](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/lib/adapters/http.js#L71) (`headers['User-Agent'] = 'axios/' + pkg.version;`)
if that's the case then i'd assume that axios is potentially sending the wrong version (the project's it's used in) in the user agent header, too?

body:
Doesn't this break proxy support when redirection occurs? 

[The setProxy function](https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/3852/files#diff-586c04c24608b86a074073c5514cc195be5c4c87ddb56da233f6d998ada4159fR40), which is called before hitting this line, sets `options.beforeRedirect` to re-apply proxy configuration after a redirect. This line here happily stamps over it. 

Either there should be something to harmonize the two features (such as registering a function that invokes both the original config beforeRedirect if needed, and the proxy re-configuration next) or the documentation should state that the `config.beforeRedirect` option is incompatible with proxy support (😿) and can introduce proxy redirect issues.

author: Edmu

body:
Interesting, looks like both variants work for passing as parameter. But only the intersection version allows you to actually access the properties. So for example, when you use a union type, you couldn't create the object first and then set properties on it individually or conditionally:

```ts
const config: AxiosInstanceConfig = { headers: {} };
config.headers.common = { "Accept-Language": "en-US" }; // error
```
This works fine with an intersection.

From my perspective, the intersection is the right thing because here, `headers` is an object that _is_ both `Partial<HeadersDefaults>` _and_ `AxiosRequestHeaders` at the same time.

See also https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?exactOptionalPropertyTypes=true# for an example showing the difference of how intersection and union types behave in this regard.

body:
To use the right protocol defined by environment variable-set proxies on redirect, `setProxy` now overrides the `options.protocol` when needed. That allows us to simplify this logic a bit, but requires moving the `options.agent` assignment to after we set the proxy.

By the way, is it me or is the `agent` only necessary when `maxRedirects` is set to 0? Unless I'm mistaken, `httpsFollow/httpFollow` use `agents.https`/`agents.http`.

This `headers.host` assignment was done two different ways:
- When initializing the request: https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/4436/files?w=1#diff-586c04c24608b86a074073c5514cc195be5c4c87ddb56da233f6d998ada4159fL216

I moved this here because it's now possible to have different effective proxying on redirects when re-resolving the proxy from environment variables - ie set for `http_proxy` but not set for `https_proxy`, or skipping due to `no_proxy` for one call but not a redirect, etc.

body:
Added tests are excellent and valuable 🙌. 

At present I suggest we don't recommend auto-serialization of form-data as the default method of choice. Instead, let's move it to be after the manual section and say that we support it now. After we have more tests, and after it is well accepted by the community, let's adapt and recommend it by default. 
Currently, conversion of files in node will not work. This is solved by https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/4469 but tests and feedback are needed in this area. 

This Pr goes way beyond adding tests to FormData payload as the title suggest. It includes FormData documentation, a whole section of documentation about AbortController, adding import from "form-data" to "Node" only, and what seems like unrelated changes to scripts (`cross-env`). I guess it is obvious why this is less than ideal. 
While the contribution is great it would be even better if it will be separated to PRs that are scoped to a certain topic/domain.
